entities.summary: César de Bus was a French Catholic priest and founder of two religious congregations, born in Cavaillon, France, in 1544 and died in 1607. He was a key figure in the development of Catholicism in 16th-century France, and his work had a significant impact on the country's religious landscape. De Bus was also a prominent theologian and writer, and his writings were widely read and studied during his lifetime. His congregations, which he founded in 1580, were dedicated to serving the poor and promoting Catholic devotion. De Bus's legacy continued to be felt in France and beyond, and he remains an important figure in the history of French Catholicism.
